text:
## Abstract  
We investigated whether raw sequencing reads are available for the GEO Series GSE309890—an RNA-seq study of *Escherichia coli* K-12 MG1655 exposed to the antidepressant sertraline—and whether these data are suitable for running a de-novo assembly. Using GEO metadata (geo_series) followed by an NCBI SRA project query (ncbi_sra_runs_for_project), we identified six paired-end Illumina HiSeq 4000 runs (SRR36018640-SRR36018645) archived under BioProject PRJNA1363958. The runs contain 69,110,351 read pairs covering 20.7 Gbp and occupying ~5.4 GB of compressed SRA files. Because the experiment is RNA-seq (LibraryStrategy = RNA-Seq), the reads represent the transcriptome rather than genomic DNA; consequently, a genome assembly would be fragmented and incomplete, whereas a transcriptome assembler (e.g. rnaSPAdes or Trinity) would be appropriate. All six runs are publicly available, and their FASTQ files can be retrieved via the provided HTTPS links or with NCBI’s `prefetch + fasterq-dump`. The data volume is modest enough for a local workstation assembly.  

## I. Introduction  
Background. Antidepressant exposure has been implicated in accelerating antibiotic resistance in bacteria. GEO Series GSE309890 examines transcriptomic changes in *E. coli* following sertraline treatment. Researchers may wish to access raw reads to perform assemblies that could reveal novel transcripts or reconstruct operon structures.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. The availability of raw reads linked to GSE309890 and their suitability for assembly analysis had not been confirmed.  
Objective & Hypothesis. We aimed (i) to determine whether GSE309890 has publicly accessible raw sequencing reads and (ii) to assess whether these reads can be assembled into meaningful sequence contigs. We hypothesised that raw RNA-seq reads are available via SRA and that they are appropriate for transcriptome, but not whole-genome, assembly.

## II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. Sequential database interrogation: first GEO to obtain study-level metadata and linked BioProject, then SRA to enumerate run accessions and download paths.  
Materials.  
• GEO (geo_series tool)  
• NCBI SRA (ncbi_sra_runs_for_project tool)  
Procedures.  
1. geo_series(accession = “GSE309890”, list_files = true)  
2. ncbi_sra_runs_for_project(accession = “PRJNA1363958”, max_results = 100)  
Statistical Analysis.  
• Run count = number of rows returned (n = 6).  
• Total spots, bases, and file sizes were obtained by summing the respective columns of the run-info table (denominator = 6 runs).  

## III. Results  
Data Presentation.  

Table 1. SRA runs linked to GSE309890 (BioProject PRJNA1363958)  
| Run | GSM (library) | Spots (pairs) | Bases | Size (MB) | Layout | Strategy | HTTPS download (trimmed) |  
|-----|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------|---------|-----------|-------------------------|  
| SRR36018645 | GSM9284457 | 11,621,726 | 3,486,517,800 | 917 | PAIRED | RNA-Seq | …/SRR36018645.lite.1 |  
| SRR36018644 | GSM9284458 | 10,415,434 | 3,124,630,200 | 801 | PAIRED | RNA-Seq | …/SRR36018644.lite.1 |  
| SRR36018643 | GSM9284459 | 11,720,219 | 3,516,065,700 | 926 | PAIRED | RNA-Seq | …/SRR36018643.lite.1 |  
| SRR36018642 | GSM9284460 | 11,992,461 | 3,597,738,300 | 955 | PAIRED | RNA-Seq | …/SRR36018642.lite.1 |  
| SRR36018641 | GSM9284461 | 11,997,182 | 3,599,154,600 | 948 | PAIRED | RNA-Seq | …/SRR36018641.lite.1 |  
| SRR36018640 | GSM9284462 | 11,363,329 | 3,408,998,700 | 894 | PAIRED | RNA-Seq | …/SRR36018640.lite.1 |  

Findings.  
• Six RNA-seq runs are available, totalling 69,110,351 read pairs (≈20.73 Gbp).  
• All runs are paired-end (2 × 150 bp) from an Illumina HiSeq 4000 platform.  
• Compressed SRA file volume is ~5.4 GB, suitable for local download.  

## IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. GSE309890 includes publicly accessible raw RNA-seq reads. Because the data derive from transcriptomic libraries, de-novo assembly will reconstruct expressed transcripts rather than the full *E. coli* genome.  
Context. Researchers interested in metabolic rewiring under sertraline stress can perform transcriptome assemblies (e.g. rnaSPAdes, Trinity) to identify isoforms or operon structures, followed by differential expression or variant calling.  
Limitations.  
• RNA-seq data omit intergenic and low-expression regions, making them unsuitable for complete genomic assembly.  
• The SRA “lite” files linked above contain reduced-quality scores; use `prefetch` to retrieve full `.sra` files if base-quality–aware assembly is required.  
• No peer-reviewed publication is yet linked; functional interpretation of assembled transcripts will require additional validation.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. Raw reads for GSE309890 are available and can support transcriptome assembly pipelines. For genome assembly, complementary DNA-seq data would be necessary. Future work could include: (i) performing rnaSPAdes assembly of each sample, (ii) mapping contigs to the *E. coli* reference to identify novel transcripts, and (iii) integrating differential expression with assembled operon structures to elucidate PPP rewiring under sertraline exposure.

## References  
[1] GEO. GSE309890 Series record. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890  
[2] NCBI SRA esearch call for PRJNA1363958. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?term=PRJNA1363958&retmax=100&retstart=0&sort=relevance&usehistory=y&retmode=json&db=sra  
[3] NCBI SRA efetch runinfo for PRJNA1363958. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?rettype=runinfo&retmode=text&retmax=100&WebEnv=MCID_6aac5525c2ad1ff3e8027b84&query_key=1&retstart=0&db=sra  

## Acknowledgments  
We thank NCBI GEO and NCBI SRA for providing open access to transcriptomic data that enabled this analysis.
